cards.front: Recall a key point about Dramatic Devices and Conventions
cards.back: Dramatic irony: audience knows something characters don't — creates tension, humour or foreboding.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Dramatic Devices and Conventions
cards.back: Soliloquy: character alone on stage speaking thoughts — reveals inner truth to audience.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Dramatic Devices and Conventions
cards.back: Aside: character briefly shares thoughts with audience — conspiratorial, breaks fourth wall.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Dramatic Devices and Conventions
cards.back: Cross-cutting: switching between two scenes — creates contrast, parallel or tension.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Dramatic Devices and Conventions
cards.back: Juxtaposition: placing contrasting elements side by side — highlights differences, creates shock or comedy.

cards.front: What should you know about drama exam tips?
cards.back: When writing about dramatic devices, use the formula: Device name + How it works + Why the playwright chose it + Effect on audience. E.g. 'The playwright uses dramatic irony when Sheila confesses but Mrs Birling doesn't realise, creating frustration and highlighting the theme of collective responsibility.'
Audience knows more than characters (e.g. Tension, anticipation)
Character speaks inner thoughts (e.g. Reveals private truth)
Object represents abstract idea (e.g. Layers of meaning)
Hints at future events (e.g. Inevitability, tension)
Character speaks to audience (e.g. Breaks illusion, intimacy)

Students often make mistakes here. Wrong: Dramatic devices are just tricks to make the play more interesting — they don't have deeper meaning. Correct: Dramatic devices are deliberate artistic choices that shape meaning. Dramatic irony in An Inspector Calls isn't just 'interesting' — it exposes the Birlings' hypocrisy. How does the playwright use at least three dramatic devices to communicate the themes of the play? Refer to a text you have studied.

Dramatic devices questions test AO1 (recall terminology) and AO2 (analyse how they create meaning). The written exam (Component 1: Understanding Drama) has Section A on a set text and Section B on live theatre. Device questions appear in Section A. You must show both knowledge of the device AND perceptive analysis of its effect.
